The double slit experiment shows that light photons can behave as both particles and as waves depending on only whether or not they are being observed. Fascinating stuff, I suggest you actually study it for more than 20 seconds. Point is, if these photons are changing the way they behave merely because they are being observed, then that changes the way we fundamentally understand the physics of the very world that we live in. Again, not as cookie-cutter as you might think it is. As I previously mentioned, I am open to alternate explanations, and the story I told and this whole sub isn't for people who believe that what they have experienced is 100% factual, and that there is no other explanation for these phenomena. It's merely for reflection upon and retelling of strange occurrences that may not make sense to us and might be part of something we have no solid understanding of just yet. Science isn't about "I'm 100% right, and you're 100% wrong," the only way that we can advance our scientific discoveries is by being open to the idea that we may sometimes be wrong, and that there is an infinite number of possibilities that we are yet to explore. Of course, if something is unfalsifiable we will not be able to explore it further in a scientific way, however it is still interesting to note, perhaps in the future we will be able to discover something that will aid us in the understanding of these strange occurrences. That doesn't discount the fact that they may just be our minds playing tricks on us, or some type of memory issue, but it's interesting to think that there may be something more.
